wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the product is an in-process library, so a refusal is an exception or a no-op and the security tests accept either; a crash cannot be told apart from a clean refusal.

traps.shape: the path grammar accepts a dot string, a bracket/quoted string and an array path (whose elements may themselves be arrays); a check written on the raw string or on a copied segment misses the array and bracket forms, so the guard has to run on the parsed, string-coerced segments
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the library's own callers pass literal dotted paths, so a check on the dot form looks sufficient and the other notations read as a separate parser feature

traps.shape: bulk configuration assignment flattens its payload into dotted keys and then sets each key; a nested prototype object arrives as one flattened key string, so a check placed on the raw payload or on the per-segment split of the payload never runs, and the flattened key reaches the same path writer
traps.reason_to_dismiss: bulk assignment is patching configuration with data already destined to become configuration, and the flattening helper is an ordinary serializer, so the report about the path writer looks like it already covers it

traps.shape: the setter factory is a second path writer: it builds closures that read and assign into their context directly and never calls the shared writer, so a guard added to the reported writer leaves it open, and it must keep auto-creating missing intermediate objects
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the factory's path is normally a developer literal at the call site and the exploder is fed the keys of a data object, so it reads as internal plumbing rather than a request-reachable sink

traps.shape: deep merge is a separate write implementation: it recurses into the existing value of every enumerable source key, and for a plain target the prototype-hook key resolves to the shared prototype, so the merge writes there without ever calling the guarded writer; its guard must keep null replacement, array identity and ordinary data keys that merely share a built-in member name
traps.reason_to_dismiss: merge is a deep-copy helper for combining two in-memory objects, not the path setter the report names, and its callers are expected to pass trusted objects
